old_title: Nottinghamshire v Leicestershire, Essex v Sussex: county cricket, day four - live
new_title: Notts draw with Leicestershire; Kent, Sussex and Durham win: county cricket, day four - as it happened
old_text:
At Chelmsford, Critchley and Snater are keeping things perky. Snater has whacked three fours and a six in his 23 since arriving. The equation is still hugely in Sussex's favour though - 79 needed, two wickets left.
A glance at the other promotion-chasing game. Kent have winkled out their first Worcestershire batsman of the day, Hasan Mahmud honing in on Adam Hose's pads, gone for 38. Worcs, 121-4, need another 259.
Unfortunately for Leicestershire, here comes Olly Stone, and he nearly grabs a wicket immediately but a diving Jack Haynes can't quite hold on at full stretch at slip. Leics 279-9.
It looks gorgeous at Trent Bridge. A diagonal shadow is coming off Cox at the non-striker's end as he watches Holland bat a ball from Pennington (4-44) into the ground. Ah, make that 5-44, as Holland edges to slip next ball. Leicestershire 259-8 - 43 to avoid the follow-on.
Ominous skies outside my window, but play has started on time everywhere.
The Met Office is optimistic: "A bright and breezy start. Chilly in places too. A few showers around during the day, mainly in the north, otherwise plenty of fine weather with some sunny spells. Feeling pleasantly warm in the sunshine, and as winds ease."
All eyes to Trent Bridge, where Leicestershire need 52 to avoid the follow-on, but lost anchor-man Josh Hull for 97.
This was Hull last night:
"I've never been in that situation before, playing an innings like that. I haven't really had the opportunity, so it was all pretty new to me. At the start, the message was just about taking it spell by spell, just bat time, trying to get the ball a bit softer, get the bowlers tired.
"I never felt it got easier, to be honest. There were times when I was seeing the ball a bit better, getting used to the bowlers and I was, like, okay, this is quite fun. And when the second new ball came along, it was dark, under lights, and the ball was nipping and zooming around a lot and it was tough.
"Obviously, I'm a bit gutted not to get to the hundred, but it was something I never really thought about the whole way through. I never really thought I had it in me to play that kind of innings. When I got to 50, and I was like, oh, this is quite cool, I'm happy with that.
"The same coming back out at 60, and then it happened pretty quick, I was suddenly on 90. When I was about 95, I started to think it could happen. But I was trying to very much just think about the game still and what got me to that position. That was my process, just trying to just face as many balls as I could."
Round-up: Somerset's Championship dream alive as Surrey sneak thriller
Somerset's dreams of a first Championship pennant continue to bubble and squeak, for now sitting pretty at the top of the table with just three rounds to go. The innings victory over Glamorgan, while Nottinghamshire were hamstrung by the weather and a stoical Leicestershire, put the spring in a west country step.
There were three wickets each for the on-song Jack Leach, Craig Overton and Lewis Gregory, the main resistance coming from Asa Tribe and Sean Dickson, who both made forties, but it was all over before tea.
But Warwickshire were close on their tails after mopping up at Southampton. A match that had started grubbily for Hampshire with the signing and unsigning of Scott Kuggeleijn finished with them dismissed for 115 and 154 to lose by an innings, flailing below the pack at the bottom of Division One. Chris Woakes whipped out both openers cheaply in Hampshire's second innings and Manav Suthar pocketed four.
There was a high-wire finish at the Oval as Surrey snookered Yorkshire by one wicket and with it the spoils of 19 points to leapfrog them and out of the relegation zone. Surrey's pursuit of 185 was stop-start-stop and when Ollie Pope went for a 12 that contained only two scoring shots and Ben Foakes was done by a Ben Coad chestnut before lunch, Surrey looked shot. But while Josh Blake's stoical 43 off 183 balls blocked one end, the tail played shots at the other. With Surrey eight wickets down, and eight runs needed, Auqib Nabi trumpeted Coad out of the ground but was out next ball. Ten scoreless deliveries followed until Dan Worrall finally hoiked a boundary to win.
The wretched season at Old Trafford rolled on, as Tom Helm (four for 36) and co bowled Middlesex to victory. After a promising start in pursuit of 297, Lancashire crumpled, losing seven for 39. George Balderson had earlier grabbed five for 54 as Middlesex spiralled in a similar manner, buoyed up by a sing-song 37 from Toby Roland-Jones.
Nottinghamshire's campaign was held up by the unlikely figure of the Leicestershirefast bowler Josh Hull, who came in as nightwatcher at Trent Bridge on Thursday night, and had only reached double figures three times in 34 innings. He was finally out after more than five hours at the crease for 97.
Good morning! Après le déluge, we still have five cracking games on our hands, the most intriguing at Trent Bridge. Can Leicestershire hold on against Stone, Pennington et al? We'll be here all day, do join us.
new_text:
To the peeling of bells in the West Country, Leicestershire played out a draw at Trent Bridge, meaning that Nottinghamshire drop behind leaders Somerset in the Championship table, albeit by just four points.
Josh Hull's 97 on Friday proved only the tip of Leicestershire's tail as the last wicket pair of Tom Scriven and Josh Davey added 106, passing the follow-on and then continuing past lunch. Haseeb Hameed just had time to make his second century of the season before the teams shook hands. The draw also improves Leicestershire's chances of survival, in the relegation zone but just seven points behind Yorkshire.
Sussex completed victory over Essex in an hour and 20 minutes to tuck their feet under the mid-table of respectability. But it wasn't without a scare or two as Matt Critchley threw the grand piano at their bowlers, last man out for 96. James Coles, who has had a quiet season after the Hundred hoohah, finished with seven wickets in the match and a valuable 79. Essex now look nervously at the the three matches ahead.
Northamptonshire had just gained ironic applause for reaching 50 from the Wantage Road crowd when they were all out in 22.2 overs. Callum Parkinson was the chief destroyer with six for 20 as Durham hit cruise control towards promotion. Northants' chances of joining them were dealt a double blow when Kent finally winkled out Worcestershire, despite a doughty unbeaten century from Brett D'Oliveira. Kent tuck in behind Durham, 15 points clear of Northants
Derbyshire folded like a damp newspaper in the face of Gloucestershire's Sai Kishore (five for 20), losing a eye-watering 10 wickets in the final session of the match, bowled out for 105. Earlier James Bracey and Miles Hammond had both danced to centuries, Bracey becoming the first Gloucestershire keeper since Harry Smith in 1919 to make two hundreds in a game. A visibly thrilled Gloucestershire, who were 37 for five on day one, have won just two games this season, both of them against Derbyshire.
There was something in the ether this round - five scores below 120, though Northants snatch the booby prize after just scraping to 50. You'll just about time to clean your teeth before we're back on Tuesday, at 10.30am. Thanks for your company, have a lovely evening.
A pinch-me-crazy match. Derbyshire have lost ten wickets in a session. Bottom of the table Gloucestershire have now won twice this season, both times against Derbyshire. Sai Kishore leads Gloucestershire off with 5 for 20. Fletch calls Derbyshire's batting "abject."
Bristol: Gloucestershire 237 and 359-5dec BEAT Derbyshire 278 and 105 by 213 runs.
Lancs v Gloucestershire is suddenly more spicy on Tuesday.
Super bowling change by Bancroft as Ollie Price comes back and immediately gets Morley lbw, despite an pitcure-book straight bat. Bashir and Randell have eight and a half overs to survive. Derby 92-9.
But now Martin Andersson, who had nearly half the score with 37, must walk into the shadows, pushing forward and gobbled up at first slip by Cameron Bancroft. Derbyshire 85-8.
Andersson and Aitchison have batted out eight overs as Ollie Price takes a break. The long armed Ed Middleton has a go. I'm going to start writing up, but will keep an eye on events at Bristol.
To the peeling of bells in the west country, they've called it a day at Trent Bridge, after HH scored his second century of the season, an unbeaten 109. The draw means Notts drop to second in the table, though just four behind Somerset. Leicestershire remain in the relegation duo, but are just seven behind Yorkshire.
Trent Bridge: Notts 451-8dec and 178-1 DRAW with v Leicestershire 365
And another...Kishore magics a bunch of flowers that turns into a slippery soap bar when it gets near to Brooke Guest who is bewildered, Derbyshire 51-6.
Wicket number four for Kishore as Donald is bowled. Derby, who are the only side to have lost to Gloucestershire this year, are in danger of a unenviable double.
A third wicket for Matt Milnes as Adam Finch fences to third slip . Three also for Mahmud and Dudgeon. Dolly undefeated on 103 and applauded off the ground. Advantage Kent.
Canterbury: Kent 238 and 358 BEAT Worcestershire 217 and 295 by 84 runs
A first hundred of the season! Full-throated applause from somewhere, I'm guessing the dressing room. Kent's target drops to two figures. Canterbury is bathed in sunshine.
Belatedly, the reason Durham weren't playing Carse this match was because he "is rested for this fixture due to pre-arranged workload management with the ECB." Which seems a bit odd, especially as he wasn't picked for the white-ball series.
Northants' headcoach Darren Lehman isn't pulling any punches: "That's the worst batting performance I've had as a coach in my time because we just didn't withstand any pressure. I mean, I got bowled out for 60 when Stuart Broad got eight for 15, and actually, he bowled beautifully that day, and we didn't play and miss. And the Aussies actually didn't bat too bad that day.
"But this performance, especially against spin, we've played spin well all year. A couple of good balls, a couple of poor decisions, and that can happen when you get bowled out for 50.
"If we want to play Division One cricket, that's the standard you got to withstand, and we haven't done that both times we've played them [this year]. So that's a challenge for the group. You know, you get to a level, but we've got to be better than that.
"But take nothing away from Durham. They're a Division One side., I'm surprised they're in this division, and they won't be now. They'll be straight up, and they'll contend for the Division One title next year."
As flagged BTL, Leus Du Plooy, is to leave Middx after three seasons after recommitting to his native South Africa. That means he can no longer be played as a local player, thus invalidating his original deal. Since joining, he has played in 38 first-class games, scoring 2795 runs at an average of 51.75, with seven centuries and a highest score of 263, against Gloucestershire.
While the Canterbury crowd were in danger of drifting off, Keith Dudgeon, who has been skulking around the outfield all day, sends Waite's stumps flying. A big, fat, inside edge -out for 37. Worcs 265-6.
Well played! He becomes the first Gloucestershire batter since 2007 to scores hundreds in both innings of a match, and the first Gloucestershire keeper to tonk them since Harry Smith in 1919.
Marcus North said, ""Aneurin Donald and Henry Crocombe are two promising players who have earned their places on the back of impressive performances in domestic cricket.
"Aneurin has had an exceptional season for Derbyshire in the Vitality Blast and also with Trent Rockets in The Hundred while Henry is a player we have had an eye on all summer."
He steps, flicks and is caught by Montgomery, a second wicket for Andersson. Boorman soon follows for a nine-ball one. A super innings by Hammond that should have saved Gloucestershire from defeat number 10. James Bracey 86 not out.
At last! McCann sprints in and trapping Scriven lbw for 54, leaving Davey unbeaten on 49. Leicestershire, from 23-2, 365 all out, trail by just 86. Fireworks from Notts approaching?
More praise for Henry Crocombe, this time from Essex captain Tom Westley:
"Crocombe has that X factor where he can change a game and he showed us that in this game. He bowls at high speed which is a challenge in itself. But that was the defining moment in the match. It's hard to swallow. I think we played good cricket for a large percentage of the game but when you have 30 minutes like that it turns the game on its head."
Three games to take us to tea. Scriven and Davey are rather amusingly adhesively attached to the Trent Bridge crease.
Hammond and Bracey press on at Bristol, Gloucs 302-3 have a lead of 261 over Derby.
And Mahmud has whistled out another Worcestershire batter as the tension builds at Canterbury. Worcs, five down, need 151. Backbone D'Oliverira not out 76.
Sneaked under the bar while the pots and pans were crashing down at Wantage Road and Chelmsford. Well played, and to James Bracey, who is undefeated on 64.
Northants 50 all out in 22.2 overs. Durham win by 153 runs
A slash to first slip puts the full stop on a dismal morning for Northants that could have huge repercussions on the rest of their season. Stokes 2-9, Parky 6-20, Potts 2-13.
Wantage Road: Durham 205 and 261 BEAT Northamptonshire 263 and 50 by 153 runs
